translation.title: Ahu Akivi, Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau and Tahai
translation.lead: Seven moai at Ahu Akivi, the unrestored Hanga Pukure platform, the red tuff of Puna Pau and the ceremonial complex of Tahai.
included: Private excursion with an English-speaking guide.
notes: A Russian-speaking guide is available for an additional charge.

hero.alt: A row of stone moai on the Ahu Akivi platform, Easter Island, Chile
hero.hover: Ahu Akivi: moai on a grassy hillside

translation.body:
Travel to the restored Ahu Akivi platform in the centre of the island, home to seven moai. According to legend, they represent seven explorers sent to Rapa Nui by King Hotu Matu'a. Continue to the unrestored platform at Ahu Hanga Pukure.

Red volcanic tuff was quarried at Puna Pau to make the topknots worn by moai. The green slopes of the quarry reveal another part of the story behind these monumental stone figures.

The route concludes at the Tahai ceremonial complex, which comprises three main platforms: Ko Te Riku, whose statue has restored eyes, Tahai and Vai Uri. This archaeological site forms part of Rapa Nui National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
